statement.p: Find a vector parametric equation for the line perpendicular to the surface z = 4 x^2 + y^2 at the point (-1,1,5).

static.solution: f(x,y,z) = 4 x^2 + y^2 - z. Then the surface z = 4 x^2 + y^2 is a level surface of f at the value 0. The gradient of f is perpendicular to the level surface. \nabla f(-1,1,5) = (8 x\,\vec i + 2 y\,\vec j - \vec k)\bigg|_{(-1,1,5)} = -8\,\mathit{\vec i}+2\,\mathit{\vec j}-\,\mathit{\vec k}. So a possible parameterization is \vec r(t) = -\left(1+8t\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}+\left(1+2t\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}+\left(5-t\right)\,\mathit{\vec k}.
